The statement is a conditional consequence of the observable and probability postulate P2 and the model postulates P5 and P6 and the cited mathematics; it asserts no joint position-momentum statistics, no dynamics, no apparatus or detector realization, no species identification and no empirical result.

items.title: Translation covariance of the massive spin-s kinematics and of its bounded-potential dynamics
items.statement:
Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and internal-factor postulate P6 read
through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] for a particle
of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's
state space with componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ and translations
$T_{a}:=T_{a}^{(r)}$ ($r=2s+1$) of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c), let
$\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law of an assigned sharp
observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$, and let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$
be real, bounded and measurable with $V_{a}(x):=V(x-a)$; write
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
for the model's free-plus-bounded-potential energy operator
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c) applied componentwise, assembled by
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]), with flow
$U_{V}(t)=\exp(-itH_{V}/\hbar)$ in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b). Then:

(a) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ the operator $T_{a}$ is unitary,
$T_{a}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$, $T_{a}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k})$, and
$$T_{a}Q_{j}T_{a}^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}P_{k}T_{a}^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(b) **Outcome-law covariance.** For every unit $\psi\in H_{s}$ and Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{T_{a}\psi}(B)=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B-a_{j}),\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{T_{a}\psi}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B):$$
translating the preparation by $a$ translates the position law by $a$ and
leaves every momentum law unchanged;

(c) **Dynamics covariance.** With $H_{V}$ and $H_{V_{a}}$ the energy operators
of the potentials $V$ and $V_{a}$,
$$T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}},\qquad T_{a}U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}=U_{V_{a}}(t)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R);$$
in particular, if $V$ is invariant under translation by $a$ (equivalently
constant almost everywhere when this holds for every $a$), then $T_{a}$ leaves
$H_{V}$ and its flow invariant, and the free flow ($V=0$) commutes with every
translation;

(d) **Frame reading.** The model reads the inertial-frame change
$t'=t$, $x'=x+a$ of P5 (a change of spatial origin; the parameter $a$ has the
unit of length, [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]) on state
representatives by $\psi'(x')=\psi(x'-a)=(T_{a}\psi)(x')$; this is the
translation convention of the model, consistent with P5's frame class, and
clauses (b) and (c) are its covariance consequences for the outcome laws and
for the bounded-potential dynamics;

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited
mathematics, and it concerns the componentwise massive model with real bounded
measurable potentials only; singular or unbounded potentials, confined or
boundary realizations, massless and relativistic models and radiation are
separate model assumptions for which no translation covariance is asserted.
No apparatus, laboratory identification or empirical result is recorded.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P2, P4, P5, P6 read through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the state space $H_{s}$ with $r=2s+1$; the operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$; the translations $T_{a}$; a real bounded measurable $V$; a unit vector $\psi$; $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$; $\lambda\in\mathbb R$; Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$.

[F1] **Componentwise kinematics.** $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are self-adjoint with the maximal componentwise domains; the translations $T_{a}$ are unitary with $T_{a}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$, $T_{a}Q_{j}T_{a}^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I$, $T_{a}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k})$, $T_{a}P_{k}T_{a}^{-1}=P_{k}$; on Schwartz classes $T_{a}$ is the shift and $P_{k}f=-i\hbar D_{k}f$ ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clauses (a),(c), [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]]).

[F2] **Laws and spectral measures.** The outcome law of an assigned sharp observable is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$; the spectral measures of the model are $E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}$ and $E_{P_{k}}(B)=U^{(s)-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{B}(p_{k})}U^{(s)}$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b), [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clauses (a),(c), [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clause (b), [[def-projection-valued-measure]]).

[F3] **Bounded-potential energy and flow.** For a real bounded measurable $V$ the operator $(1/2m)\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V}$ is self-adjoint on $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with domain invariant under the flow $e^{-itH/\hbar}$, which is a strongly continuous unitary group solving $i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H\psi(t)$ exactly on the domain ([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]] clause (c), [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]], [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-schrodinger-picture-flow]] clauses (a)-(c), [[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). The generator of a strongly continuous unitary group determines the group ([[thm-stone-one-parameter-unitary-groups]], [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).

[F4] **Multipliers shift.** $T_{a}M_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=M_{V_{a}}$ with $V_{a}(x)=V(x-a)$, and $T_{a}W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}) =W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, because the componentwise translation preserves the weak derivative and shifts the pointwise multiplier ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c), [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (c)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; read clause (a) from the componentwise translation identities, compute the law transport from the explicit multiplication and momentum-multiplier forms of the spectral measures, and conjugate the bounded-potential Hamiltonian and its flow, identifying the generator of the conjugated group.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Operators and domains] Clause (a) is exactly [F1]: unitarity of $T_{a}$, the domain equalities and the two conjugation identities. [F1]

1.2 [Position-law transport] By [F2], both sides of $E_{Q_{j}}(B)T_{a}=T_{a}E_{Q_{j}}(B-a_{j})$ are componentwise multiplication operators: for a class $f$, $\bigl(E_{Q_{j}}(B)T_{a}f\bigr)(x)=\mathbf 1_{B}(x_{j})f(x-a)$ and $\bigl(T_{a}E_{Q_{j}}(B-a_{j})f\bigr)(x) =\mathbf 1_{B-a_{j}}(x_{j}-a_{j})f(x-a) =\mathbf 1_{B}(x_{j})f(x-a)$, so the operators agree. Taking norms and using unitarity of $T_{a}$ and the law formula [F2], $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{T_{a}\psi}(B)=\|E_{Q_{j}}(B)T_{a}\psi\|^{2} =\|E_{Q_{j}}(B-a_{j})\psi\|^{2}=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B-a_{j})$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.3 [Hamiltonian covariance] By [F1], $T_{a}P_{k}T_{a}^{-1}=P_{k}$, hence also $T_{a}P_{k}^{2}T_{a}^{-1}=P_{k}^{2}$ with domain invariance; and [F4] gives $T_{a}M_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=M_{V_{a}}$, with $T_{a}W^{2,2}=W^{2,2}$. Therefore $T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}}$ as operators with domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$. [F1, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Momentum-law invariance] By [F2], $U^{(s)}E_{P_{k}}(B)U^{(s)-1}=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}(p_{k})}$ and $U^{(s)}T_{a}U^{(s)-1}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$ ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clause (d)); the two multipliers commute, so $E_{P_{k}}(B)T_{a}=T_{a}E_{P_{k}}(B)$ and $\mu^{P_{k}}_{T_{a}\psi}(B)=\|E_{P_{k}}(B)T_{a}\psi\|^{2} =\|E_{P_{k}}(B)\psi\|^{2}=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)$. Together with step 1.2 this proves (b). [step 1.2, F1, F2, algebra]

2.2 [Flow covariance] Define $W(t):=T_{a}U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}$. It is a strongly continuous unitary group because $U_{V}$ is one and conjugation by the unitary $T_{a}$ preserves the group law, unitarity and strong continuity. For $x\in D(H_{V_{a}})=T_{a}D(H_{V})$ one has $T_{a}^{-1}x\in D(H_{V})$ and $\frac1t\bigl(W(t)x-x\bigr) =T_{a}\frac1t\bigl(U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}x-T_{a}^{-1}x\bigr) \longrightarrow T_{a}\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}x\Bigr) =-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_{V_{a}}x,$ using the generator property of $U_{V}$ [F3] and step 1.3; the limit exists exactly on $D(H_{V_{a}})$ because the limit for $U_{V}$ exists exactly on $D(H_{V})$ [F3]. Hence $W$ is a strongly continuous unitary group with generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_{V_{a}}$; by [F3] the group $t\mapsto U_{V_{a}}(t)=\exp(-itH_{V_{a}}/\hbar)$ has the same generator, and uniqueness of the group with a given generator gives $T_{a}U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}=U_{V_{a}}(t)$. If $V$ is invariant under translation by $a$ then $V_{a}=V$ almost everywhere and $T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V}$ with $T_{a}U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}=U_{V}(t)$; the free case $V=0$ is translation invariant for every $a$. This proves (c). [step 1.3, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Frame reading and scope] Clause (d) records the model's convention for the passive spatial translation of P5: the parameter $a$ is the shift of the spatial origin and the representative transforms by the shift $T_{a}$, so steps 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 are exactly the transformations of the law and of the bounded-potential dynamics under the frame change. Clause (e) records the hypotheses actually used: P2, P4, P5 and P6, the componentwise model, real bounded measurable $V$ and the cited mathematics; nothing was used about singular potentials, boundaries, massless or relativistic models, radiation, apparatus or measurements. [given, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 1.3, step 2.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **Sign of the shift.** The convention is that translating the preparation by
  $a$ moves the position law by $+a$: clause (b) says
  $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{T_{a}\psi}(B)=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B-a)$. Momentum laws are
  invariant because the translation commutes with $P_{k}$; this is the
  kinematic statement that translations are generated by momentum, and the
  generator identification itself is the mathematical content of
  [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d).
- **What is not claimed.** No covariance of the internal factor under spatial
  transformations, no rotation or boost statement (those are separate items of
  this page), and no general covariance for potentials outside the bounded
  measurable class. The frame reading of clause (d) is a convention of the
  model and gains content only through the covariance statements (b) and (c).

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 7.1 printed pages 161-167 (PDF pages 173-179): Fourier transform conventions; Section 8.1 printed pages 173-175 (PDF pages 185-187): the one-parameter translation group with generator the momentum component

items.physical_scope: The translation covariance of the spin-s massive-particle model: the unitarity and operator conjugation identities of the componentwise translations, the resulting translation of the position law and invariance of the momentum laws, the conjugation of the free-plus-bounded-potential energy operator and of its flow, and the model's reading of a passive change of spatial origin. The statement is conditional on P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited mathematics, holds for real bounded measurable potentials only, and asserts nothing about singular or unbounded potentials, boundary realizations, relativistic models, radiation, apparatuses or empirical results.

items.title: Galilean boost covariance of the free massive spin-s model and the moving-frame reading
items.statement:
Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and internal-factor postulate P6 read
through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] for a particle
of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's
state space with componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]), let
$\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law of an assigned sharp
observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$, let
$H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ with flow
$U_{0}(t)=\exp(-itH_{0}/\hbar)$, and for real bounded measurable
$V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ let $H_{V}$ and $U_{V}$ be as in
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-translation-covariance]] with
$V_{u}(x,t):=V(x-ut)$. For $u\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and $t\in\mathbb R$ define the
**boost operator** $B_{u}(t)$ componentwise by
$$\bigl(B_{u}(t)\psi\bigr)(x):=\exp\Bigl(\frac{i}{\hbar}\Bigl(m\,u\cdot x -\frac{m|u|^{2}}{2}t\Bigr)\Bigr)\psi(x-ut).$$
Then:

(a) for every $u,t$ the operator $B_{u}(t)$ is unitary,
$B_{u}(t)^{-1}=B_{u}(t)^{*}$, and it maps $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ onto themselves;

(b) the operator identities
$$Q_{j}B_{u}(t)=B_{u}(t)\bigl(Q_{j}+ut_{j}I\bigr),\qquad P_{k}B_{u}(t)=B_{u}(t)\bigl(P_{k}+mu_{k}I\bigr)$$
hold with domains, and consequently for every unit $\psi$ and Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{B_{u}(t)\psi}(B)=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B-ut_{j}),\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{B_{u}(t)\psi}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B-mu_{k});$$

(c) **free covariance.** $B_{u}(t)U_{0}(t-s)=U_{0}(t-s)B_{u}(s)$ for all
$s,t\in\mathbb R$; in particular the freely evolved boosted preparation equals
the boost at time $t$ of the initial boosted preparation,
$$B_{u}(t)U_{0}(t)\psi=U_{0}(t)B_{u}(0)\psi\qquad(\psi\in H_{s});$$
and the conjugated free Hamiltonian identity
$$B_{u}(t)^{-1}H_{0}B_{u}(t)=H_{0}+u\cdot P+\frac{m|u|^{2}}{2}I$$
holds on $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ (in the chart velocity
$v=-u$ of clause (e) it reads $H_{0}-v\cdot P+\frac{m|v|^{2}}{2}I$), the
operator form of the frame change on the free generator;

(d) **moving-frame bounded-potential model.** For every real bounded
measurable $V$ and every $u$, the two-parameter family
$$W_{u}(t,s):=B_{u}(t)\,U_{V}(t-s)\,B_{u}(s)^{-1}$$
consists of unitaries preserving $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
for every $s\in\mathbb R$ and $\psi_{0}\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
the curve $t\mapsto W_{u}(t,s)\psi_{0}$ is differentiable into $L^{2}$ and
satisfies
$$i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=\Bigl(\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V_{u}(\cdot,t)}\Bigr)\psi(t),\qquad \psi(s)=\psi_{0};$$
it is the unique such curve in the stated class;

(e) **Frame reading and scope.** The model reads the inertial-frame change
$t'=t$, $x'=x+ut$ of P5 (the new chart moves with velocity $-u$ relative to the
old one) on state representatives by $\psi'(x',t)=(B_{u}(t)\psi(\cdot,t))(x')$;
clauses (b)-(d) are the covariance consequences of that reading for the laws
of the free model and for the bounded-potential dynamics in the moving frame.
The statement is conditional on P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited mathematics,
concerns the componentwise massive model with real bounded measurable
potentials only, and asserts no Lorentz covariance, no photon limit, no
covariance for singular or unbounded potentials and no worldline of an
unmeasured particle; no apparatus or empirical result is recorded.

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the massive-particle kinematics items
items.statement:
## What the pair establishes

The items of this pair are conditional consequences of the framework's
postulates and of the cited mathematics. [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]
founds the spin-$s$ model on the state space $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$
with the componentwise position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$;
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] proves that these
operators are self-adjoint with their maximal domains and provides the Fourier
representation and the translation identities;
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] proves the
canonical commutation relations on the Schwartz core, identifies the spectral
measures and proves that the internal factor commutes with the spatial
measures; [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] constructs the
momentum representation;
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] derives the position and momentum
outcome laws of the spin-$s$ model, including the Born density
$\|\psi(x)\|^{2}_{\mathbb C^{2s+1}}$ and the momentum density
$\|\psi_{p}(p)\|^{2}$;
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-translation-covariance]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-boost-covariance]] establish the covariance of these
laws and of the bounded-potential dynamics under the Galilean translations and
boosts of the model's frame class. All of this is conditional on P1, P2, P4,
P5 and P6 and on the cited mathematical suppliers; none of it is a statement
that any physical system is exactly described by the model.

## Empirical status of the parameters

The mass parameter $m>0$ and the spin label $s$ are model parameters: within
the framework they are declared values, and the identical-particle and spin
postulate assigns to a species its mass, spin, statistics and couplings as
empirical model parameters with uncertainty. This pair derives no value of
$m$ or $s$, records no measurement and asserts no species identification; the
units in which $m$, $\hbar$, $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are read are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and the exact defining constants
of the current SI recorded there are unit conventions, not measurements of
this framework.

## What is not claimed

The outcome laws are sharp-law statements: an exact position or momentum value
has probability zero in every preparation, finite-resolution outcomes are
Borel bins, and no detector, efficiency, resolution or sampling model is
introduced. The covariance theorems hold for the free model and for real
bounded measurable potentials; they assert nothing for singular or unbounded
potentials, confined or boundary realizations, massless particles, radiation
or relativistic matter. The internal factor is bookkeeping: it is not
identified with a spatial rotation, a classical angular momentum or a
relativistic spinor, and no empirical consequence of the spin assignment alone
is derived. The identification of the operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ with concrete
laboratory procedures remains a tested identification under the preparation
and apparatus postulate, external to this pair.

items.title: The Gaussian position and momentum packet of the massive model
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2 and the massive-particle model
postulate P5 read through
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] for a spinless particle
($s=0$, $r=1$) of mass parameter $m>0$, and assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Fix a width
$\sigma>0$ and define
$$\psi_{\sigma}(x):=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/4}e^{-|x|^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})},\qquad x\in\mathbb R^{3}.$$
Then:

(i) $\psi_{\sigma}\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with
$\|\psi_{\sigma}\|=1$, so its ray is a pure preparation of the model and
$\psi_{\sigma}\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{k})$ for all $j,k$, with
$D_{j}\psi_{\sigma}=-\sigma^{-2}x_{j}\psi_{\sigma}$;

(ii) with $U$ the momentum transform of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]], $U\psi_{\sigma}=\psi_{\sigma_{p}}$
where $\sigma_{p}:=\hbar/\sigma$, that is
$$(U\psi_{\sigma})(p)=(\pi\sigma_{p}^{2})^{-3/4}e^{-|p|^{2}/(2\sigma_{p}^{2})};$$

(iii) the position law of $Q_{j}$ in the preparation $[\psi_{\sigma}]$ has
density $(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/2}e^{-t^{2}/\sigma^{2}}$ in the coordinate
$t=x_{j}$, hence mean $0$ and variance $\sigma^{2}/2$; the momentum law of
$P_{k}$ has density $(\pi\sigma_{p}^{2})^{-1/2}e^{-p^{2}/\sigma_{p}^{2}}$ in
the coordinate $p=p_{k}$, mean $0$ and variance
$\sigma_{p}^{2}/2=\hbar^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})$; the product of the two standard
deviations is $\hbar/2$;

(iv) the joint position law of the three position observables has density
$|\psi_{\sigma}(x)|^{2}=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/2}e^{-|x|^{2}/\sigma^{2}}$, and
the momentum representative has density
$|(U\psi_{\sigma})(p)|^{2}=(\pi\sigma_{p}^{2})^{-3/2}e^{-|p|^{2}/\sigma_{p}^{2}}$
against $dp$.

The example is an exact model computation in one family of preparations; no
dynamics, detection model or empirical value is involved, and the variance
statements are properties of this family only.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A width $\sigma>0$; the action constant $\hbar>0$; the model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with $r=1$; the vector $\psi_{\sigma}$; the momentum transform $U$; a coordinate $j$ or $k$.

[F1] **Heat kernel.** $\Gamma(x,t):=(4\pi t)^{-n/2}e^{-|x|^{2}/(4t)}$ on $\mathbb R^{n}$, $t>0$ ([[def-heat-kernel]]), with $\int_{\mathbb R^{n}}\Gamma(x,t)\,dx=1$, $\Gamma$ of class $C^{\infty}$, and for every multi-index $\alpha$ a constant $C_{n,\alpha}<\infty$ with $|D^{\alpha}_{x}\Gamma(x,t)|\le C_{n,\alpha}t^{-(|\alpha|+n)/2}e^{-|x|^{2}/(8t)}$ ([[lem-heat-kernel-normalisation-scaling-and-derivatives]] clauses (i),(iii),(iv)); all first and second moments are absolutely integrable and $\int_{\mathbb R^{n}}x_{i}\Gamma(x,t)dx=0$, $\int_{\mathbb R^{n}}x_{i}x_{j}\Gamma(x,t)dx=2t\delta_{ij}$ ([[lem-first-and-second-moments-of-the-heat-kernel]]).

[F2] **Gaussian Fourier transform.** With the $2\pi$-normalized transform of [[thm-plancherel]] one has $\mathcal F_{2}(e^{-\pi t|x|^{2}})(\xi)=t^{-n/2}e^{-\pi|\xi|^{2}/t}$ for $t>0$ ([[lem-euclidean-gaussian-fourier-transform-with-two-pi-normalization]]); the momentum transform satisfies $U=D_{\hbar}\mathcal F_{2}$ with $D_{\hbar}g(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}g(p/(2\pi\hbar))$ and $(U\varphi)(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}\int e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\varphi(x)dx$ for $\varphi\in L^{1}\cap L^{2}$, $\mathcal F_{2}$ being the unitary extension of the $L^{1}$ transform ([[lem-nrqm-composites-momentum-fourier-jacobian]] clauses (a),(c), [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clause (a), [[thm-plancherel]]).

[F3] **Product integrals and domination.** Integrals of nonnegative measurable functions on products may be iterated ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]); $\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-u^{2}}du=\sqrt\pi$ ([[thm-gaussian-integral]]); and $\frac{x^{m}}{e^{ax}}\to0$ as $x\to+\infty$ for every $m\in\mathbb N$ and $a>0$ ([[thm-exponential-beats-every-polynomial]]).

[F4] **Schwartz classes and weak derivatives.** A class lies in $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ exactly when all seminorms $\sup_{x}|x^{\alpha}\partial^{\beta}f(x)|$ are finite ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]); a $C^{1}$ function whose classical partial derivatives lie in $L^{2}$ has those derivatives as weak derivatives ([[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]]).

[F5] **Outcome laws.** The position law of $Q_{j}$ in a preparation of the unit class $\psi$ is $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}|\psi(x)|^{2}dx$ and the momentum law of $P_{k}$ is $\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{\{p_{k}\in B\}}|(U\psi)(p)|^{2}dp$; the joint position law has density $|\psi|^{2}$ ([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clauses (a)-(c), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; identify $\psi_{\sigma}$ and its square with heat kernel slices, so that normalisation, smoothness, decay and all moments come from the heat-kernel items; transform the Gaussian with the published Gaussian Fourier lemma; and read the model's outcome densities and their variances from the heat-kernel moment identities.

**Given:** The data of the example and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Heat-kernel slices] Comparing exponents with [F1], $\Gamma\Bigl(x,\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2}\Bigr)=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/2}e^{-|x|^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})} =(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/4}\psi_{\sigma}(x),$ since $4\cdot\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2}=2\sigma^{2}$; and $\Gamma\Bigl(x,\frac{\sigma^{2}}{4}\Bigr)=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/2}e^{-|x|^{2}/\sigma^{2}} =|\psi_{\sigma}(x)|^{2}.$ [F1, algebra]

2.1 [Schwartz class, norm and domain] By step 1.1 and [F1] the function $\psi_{\sigma}$ is a constant multiple of the $C^{\infty}$ kernel slice $\Gamma(\cdot,\sigma^{2}/2)$, hence $C^{\infty}$, and every derivative obeys $|D^{\beta}\psi_{\sigma}(x)|\le C'_{\beta}e^{-|x|^{2}/(4\sigma^{2})}$ [F1]. For every multi-index $\alpha$, the seminorm $\sup_{x}|x^{\alpha}D^{\beta}\psi_{\sigma}(x)| \le C'_{\beta}\sup_{x}(1+|x|)^{|\alpha|}e^{-|x|^{2}/(4\sigma^{2})}$ is finite: the function is continuous on $\mathbb R^{3}$ and tends to $0$ at infinity, because $(1+r)^{m}e^{-r^{2}/(4\sigma^{2})}\to0$ as $r\to+\infty$, which follows from the substitution $x=r^{2}/(4\sigma^{2})$ in [F3]. Hence $\psi_{\sigma}\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ [F4]. Its norm is $\|\psi_{\sigma}\|^{2}=\int|\psi_{\sigma}|^{2} =\int\Gamma(x,\sigma^{2}/4)\,dx=1$ by step 1.1 and the normalisation of [F1]. The components $x_{j}\psi_{\sigma}$ lie in $L^{2}$ because $\int x_{j}^{2}|\psi_{\sigma}|^{2}dx=\int x_{j}^{2}\Gamma(x,\sigma^{2}/4)dx =\sigma^{2}/2$ by [F1]; and $D_{j}\psi_{\sigma}=-\sigma^{-2}x_{j}\psi_{\sigma}$, which lies in $L^{2}$ by the same computation, is the weak derivative by [F4]. This proves (i). [step 1.1, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

2.2 [Position density and variance] By [F5] and step 1.1, $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi_{\sigma}}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\Gamma(x,\sigma^{2}/4)dx$; writing $x=(x_{\perp},t)$ and iterating by [F3] gives the density $f(t)=e^{-t^{2}/\sigma^{2}}(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}e^{-|x_{\perp}|^{2}/\sigma^{2}}dx_{\perp} =(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/2}e^{-t^{2}/\sigma^{2}}$, the marginal of $\Gamma(\cdot,\sigma^{2}/4)$. Its mean vanishes and its second moment is $\int t^{2}f(t)dt=\int t^{2}\Gamma(t,\sigma^{2}/4)dt=\sigma^{2}/2$ by [F1]; hence the variance is $\sigma^{2}/2$. [step 1.1, F1, F3, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Momentum representative] By [F2] and the computation $\psi_{\sigma}=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/4}e^{-|x|^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}$, $U\psi_{\sigma}(p)=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/4}(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2} \mathcal F_{2}\bigl(e^{-|x|^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}\bigr)\Bigl(\frac{p}{2\pi\hbar}\Bigr);$ the Gaussian Fourier lemma with $t=(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1}$ gives $\mathcal F_{2}\bigl(e^{-|x|^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}\bigr)(\xi) =(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{3/2}e^{-2\pi^{2}\sigma^{2}|\xi|^{2}}$, and substituting $\xi=p/(2\pi\hbar)$ yields $U\psi_{\sigma}(p)=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/4}(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{3/2} e^{-\sigma^{2}|p|^{2}/(2\hbar^{2})} =\bigl(\pi(\hbar/\sigma)^{2}\bigr)^{-3/4}e^{-|p|^{2}/(2(\hbar/\sigma)^{2})},$ which is (ii) with $\sigma_{p}=\hbar/\sigma$. [step 2.1, F2, algebra]

4.1 [Momentum slice] Comparing step 3.1 with [F1], $|U\psi_{\sigma}(p)|^{2}=(\pi\sigma_{p}^{2})^{-3/2}e^{-|p|^{2}/\sigma_{p}^{2}} =\Gamma\Bigl(p,\frac{\sigma_{p}^{2}}{4}\Bigr).$ [step 3.1, F1, algebra]

5.1 [Momentum density and variance] By [F5] and step 4.1, $\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi_{\sigma}}(B)=\int_{\{p_{k}\in B\}}\Gamma(p,\sigma_{p}^{2}/4)dp$; the same marginal computation with width $\sigma_{p}$ gives density $(\pi\sigma_{p}^{2})^{-1/2}e^{-p^{2}/\sigma_{p}^{2}}$, mean $0$ and variance $\sigma_{p}^{2}/2=\hbar^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})$ by [F1]. The product of standard deviations is $\bigl(\sigma/\sqrt2\bigr)\bigl(\hbar/(\sqrt2\sigma)\bigr)=\hbar/2$. [step 4.1, step 2.2, F1, algebra]

6.1 [Joint densities and scope] The joint position density is $|\psi_{\sigma}|^{2}=\Gamma(\cdot,\sigma^{2}/4)$ and the momentum density is $|U\psi_{\sigma}|^{2}=\Gamma(\cdot,\sigma_{p}^{2}/4)$ by steps 1.1 and 4.1, which is (iv). All computations used only the heat-kernel and Fourier suppliers and the sharp outcome laws of [F5]; no dynamics, detector, sampling or empirical input entered. [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 2.2, step 5.1, F5] ∎

## Remarks

- **One family only.** The variances computed here are those of the Gaussian
  family; no inequality for general preparations is asserted by this example,
  and the numerical product $\hbar/2$ is a property of this family, not a
  universal law.
- **Internal factor.** For $s>0$ the vector $\psi_{\sigma}\otimes e_{m_{0}}$
  (one component equal to $\psi_{\sigma}$, all others zero) has the same
  position and momentum laws by the internal-factor invariance of
  [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (d).

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 2.3.2-2.3.3 and Box 2.3, printed pages 27-31 (PDF pages 35-39): the Gaussian packet's momentum-space amplitude and the Gaussian integral

The item uses the model's own sharp outcome laws; it computes no dynamics, models no measurement, asserts no uncertainty theorem for arbitrary preparations and records no empirical result.

items.title: The plane wave as a generalized momentum eigenfunctional
items.statement:
## Example

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $d\ge1$,
$\hbar>0$ and $k\in\mathbb R^{d}$, and define on the Schwartz space
$\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]] the conjugate-linear functional
$$u_{k}(\varphi):=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}e^{ik\cdot x}\,\overline{\varphi(x)}\,dx.$$
Let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the negative-sign $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform,
$\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)=\int\psi(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on
$L^{1}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Then:

(a) $u_{k}$ is well defined, conjugate-linear, and bounded in every Schwartz
seminorm in the sense that
$$|u_{k}(\varphi)|\le\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}|\varphi(x)|\,dx<\infty;$$
moreover $u_{k}(\varphi)=\mathcal F_{2}\bigl(\overline{\varphi}\bigr)\bigl(-\tfrac{k}{2\pi}\bigr)$
for every $\varphi$;

(b) for every $\varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ and every
$j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$, with $P_{j}\varphi:=-i\hbar\,\partial_{j}\varphi$ the
componentwise momentum action on Schwartz classes,
$$u_{k}(P_{j}\varphi)=\hbar k_{j}\,u_{k}(\varphi),\qquad u_{k}(P_{j}^{2}\varphi)=(\hbar k_{j})^{2}\,u_{k}(\varphi):$$
the functional is a generalized eigenfunctional of every momentum component
with eigenvalue $\hbar k_{j}$;

(c) there is no $L^{2}$ class $F\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ with
$u_{k}(\varphi)=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}F(x)\overline{\varphi(x)}\,dx$ for all
$\varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$; in particular the functions
$x\mapsto e^{ik\cdot x}$ and its nonzero scalar multiples are not elements of
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$;

(d) the statements are purely mathematical: $u_{k}$ is a conjugate-linear
functional on the Schwartz space, no normalizable class represents it, and no
physical state, preparation or outcome probability is attached to it by this
example.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice; $d\ge1$; $\hbar>0$; $k\in\mathbb R^{d}$; Schwartz classes $\varphi,\psi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$; the functional $u_{k}$; the transform $\mathcal F_{2}$; a class $F\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$.

[L1] **Schwartz classes are integrable, and the transform is an automorphism.** $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)\subseteq L^{1}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ and $\mathcal F_{2}$ maps $\mathcal S$ bijectively onto itself, continuously in the Schwartz topology; on Schwartz classes the transform is the integral $\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)=\int\psi(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]], [[cor-fourier-transform-is-a-topological-automorphism-of-schwartz-space]], no choice beyond countable choice for the $L^{2}$ extension).

[L2] **Fourier multipliers.** For $\psi\in\mathcal S$ and any coordinate $j$, $\mathcal F_{2}(\partial_{j}\psi)(\xi)=2\pi i\xi_{j}\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)$ for almost every $\xi$; both sides are Schwartz functions, hence continuous, so the identity holds for every $\xi$ ([[lem-weak-derivatives-are-polynomial-fourier-multipliers]], [[cor-fourier-transform-is-a-topological-automorphism-of-schwartz-space]]).

[L3] **Modulus one.** $|e^{i\theta}|=1$ for real $\theta$ ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]), so $|e^{ik\cdot x}|=1$ for every $x$.

[L4] **Density and monotone convergence.** $C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ is dense in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$, and if $h\in L^{2}$ satisfies $\int h\overline{v}=0$ for all $v\in C_{c}^{\infty}$ then $h=0$ ([[lem-smooth-compactly-supported-functions-are-dense-in-ltwo-of-an-open-set]]); integrals of nonnegative measurable functions on expanding boxes converge to the full integral ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; identify the functional with the $L^{1}$ Fourier transform of the conjugate test class, use the Fourier multiplier identity for the eigenrelation, and use the density of test classes and the non-integrability of the constant modulus to rule out an $L^{2}$ representative.

**Given:** The data of the example and [L1]-[L4].

1.1 [Well-definedness and continuity] For $\varphi\in\mathcal S$ the product $e^{ik\cdot x}\overline{\varphi(x)}$ has modulus $|\varphi(x)|$ by [L3] and is measurable, so the integral converges absolutely by [L1]: $|u_{k}(\varphi)|\le\int|\varphi|<\infty$. Conjugate-linearity in $\varphi$ is immediate from the definition, and $u_{k}(\varphi) =\int\overline{\varphi(x)}e^{-2\pi ix\cdot(-k/2\pi)}dx =\mathcal F_{2}(\overline{\varphi})(-k/(2\pi))$ by [L1] applied to the Schwartz class $\overline{\varphi}$. This proves (a). [L1, L3, algebra]

2.1 [Eigenrelation] Let $\varphi\in\mathcal S$ and put $\psi:=\overline{\varphi}$, a Schwartz class. Since $\overline{P_{j}\varphi}=\overline{-i\hbar\partial_{j}\varphi} =i\hbar\,\partial_{j}\overline{\varphi}=i\hbar\,\partial_{j}\psi$, one has $u_{k}(P_{j}\varphi)=\int e^{ik\cdot x}\overline{P_{j}\varphi}\,dx =i\hbar\int e^{ik\cdot x}\partial_{j}\psi(x)\,dx =i\hbar\,\mathcal F_{2}(\partial_{j}\psi)\Bigl(-\frac{k}{2\pi}\Bigr),$ where the last step evaluates the $L^{1}$ transform at $-k/(2\pi)$. By [L2], $\mathcal F_{2}(\partial_{j}\psi)(\xi)=2\pi i\xi_{j}\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)$ for every $\xi$, so at $\xi=-k/(2\pi)$, $u_{k}(P_{j}\varphi)=i\hbar\cdot2\pi i\Bigl(-\frac{k_{j}}{2\pi}\Bigr)\mathcal F_{2}\psi\Bigl(-\frac{k}{2\pi}\Bigr) =\hbar k_{j}\,u_{k}(\varphi),$ using step 1.1. Applying the same identity to $P_{j}\varphi$ (again a Schwartz class) gives $u_{k}(P_{j}^{2}\varphi)=\hbar k_{j}u_{k}(P_{j}\varphi) =(\hbar k_{j})^{2}u_{k}(\varphi)$. This proves (b). [step 1.1, L1, L2, algebra]

2.2 [No $L^{2}$ representative] Suppose $F\in L^{2}$ satisfies $\int F\overline{\varphi}=u_{k}(\varphi)$ for all $\varphi\in\mathcal S$, and put $G:=e^{-ik\cdot x}F\in L^{2}$, a class of the same norm because the multiplier has modulus one [L3]. Replacing $\varphi$ by $e^{ik\cdot x}\varphi$, which is again a Schwartz class, in the assumed identity gives $\int G\,\overline{\varphi} =\int F\,\overline{e^{ik\cdot x}\varphi} =u_{k}\bigl(e^{ik\cdot x}\varphi\bigr) =\int e^{ik\cdot x}\overline{e^{ik\cdot x}\varphi}\,dx =\int\overline{\varphi},$ that is $\int(G-1)\overline{\varphi}=0$ for every $\varphi\in\mathcal S$ and hence for every $\varphi\in C_{c}^{\infty}$; by [L4] the class $G-1\in L^{2}$ vanishes, so $G=1$ almost everywhere. But then $\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}|G|^{2}=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}1=+\infty$ by monotone convergence on expanding boxes [L4], contradicting $G\in L^{2}$. Hence no such $F$ exists. Applying the same computation to $F=ze^{ik\cdot x}$ for $z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$ shows that no nonzero scalar multiple is represented either. This proves (c). [step 1.1, L3, L4, algebra]

3.1 [Conclusion] Statement (d) records that only Schwartz classes and the functional $u_{k}$ were used; no normalizable class and no probability law is attached to $u_{k}$ by this example. [given, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **The delta normalization is formal.** Formally writing
  $u_{k}(\varphi)=\int\overline{\varphi(x)}e^{ikx}dx$ as a pairing against
  $e^{ikx}$ suggests the orthogonality symbol $\int e^{i(k-k')x}dx=2\pi\delta(k-k')$
  familiar from physics texts; the functional $u_{k}$ is the precise object,
  and the delta is a formal notation for it, not an $L^{2}$ inner product.
- **Why this is not a state.** By clause (c), no element of $L^{2}$ represents
  $u_{k}$; the framework's state assignment requires a nonzero $L^{2}$ class,
  so the plane wave is not a preparation, and no position or momentum
  probability density attaches to it. The example establishes the
  distributional eigenrelation only.

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 1 'Wave Mechanics', Section 6, printed pages 22-24 (PDF pages 22-24): momentum eigenstates are plane waves and are not normalizable

items.title: No bounded operators satisfy the canonical commutation relation with a nonzero commutator
items.statement:
## Statement refuted

Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $\hbar>0$. Then there exist
bounded linear operators $A,B\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
$$AB-BA=i\hbar I .$$

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]); a nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$; $\hbar>0$; a hypothetical pair $A,B\in\mathcal B(H)$ of bounded linear operators with $AB-BA=i\hbar I$; a vector $x\in H$; a real $t$.

[F1] **Heisenberg flow for a bounded operator.** Let $T$ be self-adjoint and $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ with $A\,D(T)\subseteq D(T)$; put $A(t):=U(-t)AU(t)$ for $U(t)=e^{itT}$. Then $A(t)\in\mathcal B(H)$, $\|A(t)\|=\|A\|$ for every $t$, and for every $y\in D(T)$ the map $t\mapsto A(t)y$ is differentiable with $\frac{d}{dt}A(t)y=-i\bigl(TA(t)-A(t)T\bigr)y$ ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a),(b)).

[F2] **Flow calculus.** $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group with $U(t)^{*}=U(-t)$, $U(t)D(T)=D(T)$ and $TU(t)=U(t)T$ on $D(T)$; if $T$ is bounded then $D(T)=H$ and these are identities of bounded operators ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a), [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

[F3] **Curves with vanishing derivative.** If $w:I\to H$ is differentiable on an interval with $w'\equiv0$, then $w$ is constant: for $s,t\in I$, $\|w(t)-w(s)\|\le\sup_{\xi}\|w'(\xi)\|\,|t-s|=0$ ([[lem-mean-value-inequality-for-a-differentiable-banach-valued-curve]]).

[F4] **Norm identities.** The operator norm is a norm on $\mathcal B(H)$, so $\|S-T\|\ge\bigl|\|S\|-\|T\|\bigr|$ and $\|cS\|=|c|\,\|S\|$ for scalars $c$ ([[def-operator-norm]], [[lem-operator-norm-is-a-norm]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

## Counterexample

**Proof technique:** direct; show that the assumed bounded commutator relation would make the Heisenberg flow of $A$ under the bounded self-adjoint generator $B$ a linear-in-$t$ family with constant norm, and let $t\to\infty$ for a contradiction with the reverse triangle inequality.

**Given:** The data of the refuted statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [The conjugated commutator] Suppose the pair $A,B$ exists. Since $B$ is bounded and self-adjoint, $D(B)=H$, and [F2] gives $BU(-t)=U(-t)B$ and $U(t)B=BU(t)$ as bounded-operator identities for the flow $U(t)=e^{itB}$. Hence $BA(t)=BU(-t)AU(t)=U(-t)BAU(t),\qquad A(t)B=U(-t)AU(t)B=U(-t)ABU(t),$ so $BA(t)-A(t)B=U(-t)(BA-AB)U(t)$; inserting the assumed $AB-BA=i\hbar I$, that is $BA-AB=-i\hbar I$, and using $U(-t)U(t)=I$, we obtain $BA(t)-A(t)B=-i\hbar\,I.$ [F2, given, algebra]

2.1 [The flow is affine in $t$] The product-domain hypothesis of [F1] holds for $A$ and the bounded self-adjoint $T:=B$, because $D(T)=H$; hence for every $x\in H$ the map $t\mapsto A(t)x$ is differentiable with $\frac{d}{dt}A(t)x=-i(BA(t)-A(t)B)x=-\hbar x$ by step 1.1. Therefore $w(t):=A(t)x+\hbar tx$ satisfies $w'(t)=0$ for all $t$ and is constant by [F3], with $w(0)=Ax$; hence $A(t)x=\bigl(A-\hbar tI\bigr)x\qquad(x\in H,\ t\in\mathbb R).$ [step 1.1, F1, F3, algebra]

3.1 [Norm contradiction] By [F1] applied to $A$ and $T=B$, $\|A(t)\|=\|A\|$ for every $t$; by step 2.1 the operator identity $A(t)=A-\hbar tI$ holds, so $\|A-\hbar tI\|=\|A\|$ for every $t$. But [F4] gives $\|A-\hbar tI\|\ge\hbar|t|-\|A\|$, which for $|t|>2\|A\|/\hbar$ exceeds $\|A\|$. This is a contradiction: no such pair $A,B$ exists. Consequently the displayed existential claim is refuted. [step 2.1, F1, F4, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Unboundedness is not a technicality.** The refutation shows that a
  canonical commutation relation with $\hbar>0$ cannot hold as an identity of
  bounded operators; at least one of the two operators must be unbounded (or
  the relation must be stated on a core, as for the model's componentwise
  operators, or replaced by the unitary Weyl form). This is why the model
  defines position and momentum on dense domains rather than on all of the
  Hilbert space.
- **What is not refuted.** A core relation such as the canonical commutation
  relations on the Schwartz classes, and the associated one-parameter unitary
  groups, are unaffected: the operators there are unbounded. This item makes
  no statement about the Weyl form, about semiboundedness, or about any
  physical system.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.1, printed pages 55-58 (PDF pages 67-70): the closed graph theorem forces observables such as position and momentum to be unbounded, with only dense domains

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Box 2.2 and Sections 2.3.1-2.3.2, printed pages 25-27 (PDF pages 33-35): the integration-by-parts Hermiticity argument for the momentum operator (wavefunctions vanishing at spatial infinity) and the canonical commutator [x,p]=i hbar

items.title: A confined model with Dirichlet walls: the naive interval momentum is not an observable
items.statement:
Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and the
kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Consider the following
hypothetical confined-model extension of the kinematics: a spinless particle
of mass $m>0$ is restricted to an interval $(0,L)$ of length $0<L<\infty$ in
one spatial direction, with Hilbert space $L^{2}(0,L;\mathbb C)$, and the
model declares its momentum to be the formal differential expression
$$T:=-i\hbar D,\qquad D(T):=\bigl\{u\in H^{1}(0,L;\mathbb C):\ u^{*}(0)=u^{*}(L)=0\bigr\},$$
with $H^{1}$ and the continuous trace $u^{*}$ as in
[[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]. Then, in that hypothetical
model:

(a) $T$ is densely defined and symmetric, but not self-adjoint; its adjoint is
$$T^{*}=-i\hbar D,\qquad D(T^{*})=H^{1}(0,L;\mathbb C),$$
without boundary condition;

(b) no self-adjoint extension $S\supseteq T$ has domain contained in the
Dirichlet class $D(T)$: there is no self-adjoint realization of the formal
momentum on $(0,L)$ that keeps the Dirichlet condition on its domain;

(c) for every self-adjoint extension $S\supseteq T$ and every $n\ge1$, the
normalized Dirichlet function $u_{n}(x)=\sqrt{2/L}\,\sin(n\pi x/L)$ lies in
$D(S)$ but is not an eigenvector of $S$; consequently a momentum
quantization read off from the Dirichlet eigenfunctions is not a statement
about any self-adjoint realization of the interval momentum;

(d) therefore $T$ is not an assigned sharp observable of the model in the
sense of P2, and no outcome law of a momentum observable of the confined
model exists until the model declares a self-adjoint realization of its
momentum. An explicit family of self-adjoint realizations of the same formal
expression is the twisted-periodic family $P_{\theta}$, $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$,
of [[thm-nrqm-intervals-twisted-periodic-momentum-domain]], whose domains
impose $u(L)=e^{i\theta}u(0)$ rather than Dirichlet conditions; nothing here
claims that any member of that family, or any other realization, describes a
laboratory apparatus.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P2 and P5 read as above; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; $0<L<\infty$; the operator $T$ of the statement; classes $u,v\in H^{1}(0,L;\mathbb C)$; a self-adjoint extension $S$ of $T$; an integer $n\ge1$; the Dirichlet function $u_{n}$.

[F1] **Interval Sobolev space and integration by parts.** $H^{1}(0,L)$ is the space of $L^{2}$ classes with an $L^{2}$ weak derivative; each class has a continuous representative, its trace $u^{*}$ is defined at the endpoints, and $-\int_{0}^{L}u\,\overline{v'} =u^{*}(0)\overline{v^{*}(0)}-u^{*}(L)\overline{v^{*}(L)} \int_{0}^{L}u'\,\overline{v}$ for all $u,v\in H^{1}(0,L)$; the test classes $C_{c}^{\infty}(0,L)$ lie in every Dirichlet class and are dense in $L^{2}$ ([[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]], [[lem-nrqm-intervals-integration-by-parts]]). In particular $D(T)\supseteq C_{c}^{\infty}(0,L)$ is dense in $L^{2}(0,L;\mathbb C)$ and $D(T)$ is a linear subspace of $H^{1}$.

[F2] **Adjoints and self-adjointness.** A densely defined operator $B$ is symmetric when $\langle Bu,v\rangle=\langle u,Bv\rangle$ for all $u,v\in D(B)$; its adjoint $B^{*}$ has domain consisting of the $v$ for which $u\mapsto\langle Bu,v\rangle$ is bounded on $D(B)$, and $B$ is self-adjoint when $B^{*}=B$ including domains; a self-adjoint operator has no proper symmetric extension ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]).

[F3] **Assigned observables are self-adjoint.** An assigned sharp observable of the framework is a pair of a densely defined self-adjoint operator and a declared unit; a symmetric formal differential expression on a smaller domain does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a)).

[F4] **Twisted-periodic realizations.** For each $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$ the operator $P_{\theta}=-iD$ with domain $D(P_{\theta})=\{u\in H^{1}(0,L):u^{*}(L)=e^{i\theta}u^{*}(0)\}$ is densely defined, symmetric and self-adjoint ([[thm-nrqm-intervals-twisted-periodic-momentum-domain]] clause (a)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the adjoint of the Dirichlet momentum by integration by parts, show that no self-adjoint extension can keep the Dirichlet domain, test the Dirichlet functions against an arbitrary self-adjoint extension, and read the observability conclusion off the self-adjointness requirement of the observable postulate.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Density and symmetry] $D(T)$ contains $C_{c}^{\infty}(0,L)$, which is dense in $L^{2}$ [F1]; hence $T$ is densely defined, and it is linear on the linear subspace $D(T)$ [F1]. For $u,v\in D(T)$, the integration-by-parts identity [F1] gives $\langle Tu,v\rangle-\langle u,Tv\rangle =-i\hbar\Bigl(u^{*}(0)\overline{v^{*}(0)}-u^{*}(L)\overline{v^{*}(L)}\Bigr)=0,$ because both traces of both functions vanish. Hence $T$ is symmetric. [F1, algebra]

2.1 [The adjoint] Let $v\in H^{1}(0,L)$. For every $u\in D(T)$, [F1] gives $\langle Tu,v\rangle=-i\hbar\int_{0}^{L}Du\,\overline{v} =-i\hbar\bigl[u^{*}\overline{v^{*}}\bigr]_{0}^{L} +\int_{0}^{L}u\,\overline{-i\hbar Dv} =\langle u,-i\hbar Dv\rangle$, since $u^{*}$ vanishes at both endpoints; so $u\mapsto\langle Tu,v\rangle$ is the restriction of a bounded functional and $v\in D(T^{*})$ with $T^{*}v=-i\hbar Dv$ [F2]. Conversely, if $v\in D(T^{*})$, testing the identity $\langle Tu,v\rangle=\langle u,T^{*}v\rangle$ against $u\in C_{c}^{\infty}(0,L)\subseteq D(T)$ shows that the distribution $-i\hbar Dv$ equals the $L^{2}$ class $T^{*}v$; hence $v$ has an $L^{2}$ weak derivative, that is $v\in H^{1}(0,L)$, and $T^{*}v=-i\hbar Dv$. Thus $D(T^{*})=H^{1}(0,L)$. The constant class $1$ lies in $H^{1}(0,L)$ with $1^{*}(0)=1\ne0$, so $D(T^{*})\ne D(T)$ and $T$ is not self-adjoint. This proves (a). [step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

2.2 [Dirichlet functions are not momentum eigenvectors] Fix $n\ge1$ and put $u_{n}(x):=\sqrt{2/L}\sin(n\pi x/L)$, a unit class in $H^{1}(0,L)$ with $u_{n}^{*}(0)=u_{n}^{*}(L)=0$, so $u_{n}\in D(T)$ and its weak derivative is the classical derivative $u_{n}'(x)=\sqrt{2/L}\,(n\pi/L)\cos(n\pi x/L)$ [F1]. Let $S\supseteq T$ be any self-adjoint extension. Then $u_{n}\in D(S)$ and $Su_{n}=Tu_{n}=-i\hbar u_{n}' =-i\hbar\sqrt{2/L}\,\frac{n\pi}{L}\cos(n\pi x/L).$ Suppose $Su_{n}=\lambda u_{n}$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb R$; then the continuous functions $\cos(n\pi x/L)$ and $\sin(n\pi x/L)$ would be proportional on $[0,L]$. At $x=0$ one has $\sin0=0$ and $\cos0=1$, so proportionality would force the sine multiple to vanish identically, a contradiction. Hence $u_{n}$ is not an eigenvector of $S$, for any self-adjoint extension $S$. This proves (c). [step 1.1, F1, algebra]

3.1 [No Dirichlet self-adjoint extension] Let $S\supseteq T$ be self-adjoint with $D(S)\subseteq D(T)$. Since $T\subseteq S$, one has $D(T)\subseteq D(S)$; with the assumed inclusion this gives $D(S)=D(T)$, and since $S$ agrees with $T$ on $D(T)$, the operators coincide: $S=T$. But then $T$ would be self-adjoint, contradicting step 2.1. Hence no such $S$ exists, which is (b). Equivalently, any self-adjoint extension of $T$ must contain a vector of $H^{1}(0,L)$ whose trace at $0$ or $L$ is nonzero. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F2, algebra]

4.1 [Observability and scope] By [F3], assigned sharp observables of the model are densely defined self-adjoint operators; by steps 1.1 and 2.1 the Dirichlet momentum $T$ is densely defined and symmetric but not self-adjoint, so $T$ is not an assigned sharp observable of the hypothetical confined model, and no outcome law of the confined momentum exists until a self-adjoint realization is declared. [F4] provides an explicit family $P_{\theta}$ of self-adjoint realizations of the same formal expression $-iD$, distinct from the Dirichlet operator; the statement neither selects a member of that family nor asserts any laboratory realization, and it makes no claim about the framework's own momentum $P$ of P5, which is defined on the full line and is not obtained by restricting $T$. This proves (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.2, F3, F4] ∎

## Remarks

- **The obstruction is the boundary form.** Symmetry of $-i\hbar D$ on a
  domain imposes $u^{*}(0)\overline{v^{*}(0)}=u^{*}(L)\overline{v^{*}(L)}$ for
  all pairs in the domain; the Dirichlet domain satisfies this only in the
  degenerate way, and enlarging it to any self-adjoint domain necessarily
  relates the endpoint values, as the twisted-periodic family illustrates
  ([[thm-nrqm-intervals-twisted-periodic-momentum-domain]]).
- **What is not claimed.** The thought experiment does not assert that
  confined models are physically realized, does not compare models with data,
  and does not claim that box energy levels lack a self-adjoint energy
  realization; the Dirichlet Laplacian is a self-adjoint energy operator, and
  the warning concerns the momentum observable only.

items.physical_scope: A conditional warning about a hypothetical confined-model extension of the massive-particle kinematics: if a model confines a spinless particle to an interval and declares the formal momentum -i hbar d/dx on the Dirichlet domain, then that operator is symmetric but not self-adjoint and hence is not an assigned sharp observable of the observable and probability postulate; no self-adjoint extension keeps the Dirichlet domain, and the Dirichlet eigenfunctions are not momentum eigenfunctions of any such extension. The item asserts no experiment, no apparatus realization and no claim that confinement models are physically realized; it excludes any assertion about which self-adjoint realization, if any, describes a laboratory device.

items.title: What the worked items of the companion page establish
items.statement:
## Three worked items

**The Gaussian packet.** [[ex-nrqm-kinematics-gaussian-position-momentum-packet]]
computes, in the spin-zero massive model, the normalized Gaussian
$\psi_{\sigma}(x)=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/4}e^{-|x|^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}$, shows
that its momentum representative is again a normalized Gaussian with width
$\sigma_{p}=\hbar/\sigma$, and evaluates the position and momentum outcome
densities of the model together with their variances $\sigma^{2}/2$ and
$\hbar^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})$ and the product $\hbar/2$. This verifies the model's
sharp laws of [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] on a family of
Schwartz preparations; it computes no dynamics, no measurement and no general
uncertainty statement.

**The plane wave as a generalized functional.** [[ex-nrqm-kinematics-plane-wave-generalized-eigenfunction]]
defines the conjugate-linear functional $u_{k}(\varphi)=\int e^{ik\cdot
x}\overline{\varphi}$ on Schwartz classes, proves the eigenrelation
$u_{k}(P_{j}\varphi)=\hbar k_{j}u_{k}(\varphi)$, and proves that no $L^{2}$
class represents $u_{k}$. This is the precise sense in which the plane wave is
a generalized momentum eigenfunction: it diagonalizes the momentum action on
the test space while carrying no state or probability density. The framework's
state assignment excludes it as a preparation, in agreement with the model's
atomless sharp laws.

**The boundary warning.** [[texp-nrqm-kinematics-dirichlet-momentum-warning]]
shows, in a hypothetical confined-model extension, that the formal interval
momentum $-i\hbar D$ on the Dirichlet domain is symmetric but not self-adjoint,
that no self-adjoint extension keeps the Dirichlet domain, and that the
Dirichlet functions are not momentum eigenfunctions of any self-adjoint
extension. The companion counterexample
[[cex-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-cannot-hold-for-bounded-operators]] shows that the
canonical commutation relation cannot hold as an identity of bounded
operators at all, so the core relation of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] is genuinely a
relation on a dense core of unbounded operators rather than a bounded
operator identity.

## What the page does not establish

None of the items is an experiment: no counts, calibration, resolution,
efficiency, background, uncertainty or data comparison appears anywhere on the
page, and no value of $m$, $\hbar$ or any model parameter is measured. The
Gaussian computation is a single family of preparations; the plane-wave item
is a distributional statement without a state; the boundary warning and the
bounded-commutator counterexample are conditional mathematical statements
about hypothetical or bounded models, not claims about apparatuses. In
particular, no item asserts that confined models, twisted-periodic momenta or
any self-adjoint realization describe a laboratory device, and no item draws
conclusions about decoherence, measurement disturbance or relativistic
effects, which belong to other model pages.
